payload.title: Where does the record live, off every code branch?
payload.body: On a crash after an event's line is in the record worktree's file and before its commit, h-ref meets the build Goal's line 3 (no command reads part of a write) and h-record-worktree does not, because a reader of that worktree sees an event that git clean or git checkout there can still lose, while under h-ref a reader sees the event only once update-ref has landed. If h-record-worktree read only commits, it would be h-ref plus a checkout that adds nothing.

why: The owner's question from the grill of 2026-11-14 (round 2, Q6), settled in session.

payload.title: The record is commits on a hidden ref, written by git plumbing and never checked out
payload.body: hyp writes each event, and the bytes of each file it names, as git objects, then moves refs/hyp/record to a new commit with update-ref; an event exists for every reader of the clone only once the ref has moved, and no worktree holds the record's files.

why: The rival the owner chose in the grill of 2026-11-14.

payload.title: The record is a branch holding only .tree/, checked out in its own worktree
payload.body: hyp appends each event to the files of a worktree that checks out a record branch, then commits them there; readers read that worktree's files (#179 question 1).

why: The rival #179 proposed, rejected in the grill of 2026-11-14.

payload.title: Settled in the grill: the crash between a record worktree's file line and its commit
payload.body: Rubric, decided by reading: walk the scenario in scenarios.md. A rival under which a reader can see an event that a later git act on a worktree loses is contradicted; a rival under which a reader sees an event only once it is durable is supported.

why: Records the owner's session decision as an Experiment with its rubric.

payload.observation: Settled by argument in the grill of 2026-11-14 with the owner: on a crash between a record worktree's file line and its commit, h-record-worktree lets a reader see an event a later git act on the worktree loses; h-ref shows an event only once update-ref lands.

why: The owner's session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.

payload.body: The build question of G-SZCBXZ. The run adds one Hypothesis per candidate commit, with its subject the base plus that commit; a fix is a new Hypothesis that supersedes the one it fixes. The base is the Hypothesis 'nothing changes': each Experiment's rubric asks for red on base and green on the candidate, except the base guards the Goal body names (line 3, the last sentence of line 9).
